about.title: Orange Cove Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Orange Cove is a small city, but property owners here still carry the same legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe as anywhere else in Fresno County — whether that's a grocery store on American Avenue, an apartment complex, or a packing facility tied to the area's agricultural economy. When a fall happens on a wet floor, a broken step, uneven pavement, or in a poorly lit parking area, the path to compensation depends on proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documenting what happened matters so much: photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage before it's overwritten can make or break a claim. LawProactive doesn't handle your case directly — we're a free service that connects injured Orange Cove residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, all on a contingency basis so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Getting Legal Help Early Matters

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help identify what evidence supports that, from maintenance logs to prior complaints.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly gives an attorney the best chance to request and preserve video before it's gone for good.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly blamed for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly so you're not shouldering more blame than you should.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim after a fall in Orange Cove?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, like a government building or city-owned lot, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility — your recovery is just reduced by your percentage of fault. This is something an attorney can help evaluate based on the specific circumstances.

items.question: I fell at a business near Hills Valley Road in Orange Cove — what should I do first?
items.answer: Take photos of exactly where and how you fell, note any wet floors, broken flooring, or poor lighting, and get names of any witnesses if possible. Ask the business to preserve any surveillance footage, and consider getting connected with an attorney soon since video is often deleted quickly.
